svg.title: Hermitian support does not imply invariance of a probability law
svg.desc: Permutation congruence swaps two distinct Hermitian matrices H and H prime. A Dirac law has weights one and zero on those two points, which become zero and one after the swap, so the law changes even though all mass remains Hermitian. A balanced two-point law has weights one half and one half before and after the swap, so it is invariant under this permutation although each sampled matrix changes. This finite law is not an intrinsic Gaussian and does not prove invariance under every unitary matrix.
svg.text: Support asks where mass lives; invariance asks how weights move
Exact two-point toy laws on the Hermitian matrices H and H' from the running example.
The permutation congruence swaps the two points
and applying it again returns H
Hermitian support before and after: mass 1. Law invariant: no, because (1,0) != (0,1).
Every point moves, but the law is unchanged under this one permutation because the weights are exchanged equally.
Boundary: this balanced finite law is not Gaussian and is not claimed invariant under every unitary congruence.
